title: Write project SOP for AI-assisted feature/data additions (prevent dead-code-yet-tested pattern)
description: Prompted by Tier 5 audit finding: vaderSentiment-dependent sentiment analysis ran successfully (tests green post-aj1) but the renderer never displayed the output. aj1 fixed tests for unused code. Same pattern likely exists elsewhere. SOP should require: (1) every new analyzer/feature includes a documented renderer-consumer mapping; (2) tests must verify data reaches the report (not just that the analyzer runs); (3) dead-code purge cadence (e.g., quarterly grep for emit-but-never-read patterns); (4) checklist for AI assistants to follow when adding features. Plan toward writing this in Tier 5 or 6 once we have more example incidents to draw from. Source: bd memory + Tier 5 audit findings 2026-04-29.

title: Missing test/runtime deps: networkx + vaderSentiment cause 11 pytest failures
description: 11 pre-existing pytest failures across test_internal_linking.py (4 — missing networkx) and test_local_seo.py (7 — missing vaderSentiment). Analyzers use try/except-import and silently degrade to empty/zero when missing. Prod data-integrity implication: if build_audit.py runs in a venv missing these libs, extended internal-link metrics (density, betweenness, communities) and review sentiment are silently zero. Reports/XLSX/PPTX consumers see blank cells. Action: confirm prod venv has these (pip show networkx vaderSentiment in prod). If yes, add to pyproject.toml as optional extras + CI-only. If no, silent prod regression — add to main dependencies. Source: HANDOFF-POST-TIER-3 Section 5b.

title: test_connectors_base 5xx + timeout retry tests fail (pre-existing)

title: Remove committed .collab/ directory (10 files incl 104KB binary collab.db)
description: Discovered during 0au v4 branch forensic investigation. The .collab/ directory (10 files) was committed in v4 at a139db9 and is currently tracked in site-audit-fixes-tier-4 (inherited). Contents: collab.db (104KB SQLite binary — runtime state artifact for a multi-LLM collaboration system), partner-prompt-claude.md, partner-prompt-codex.md, partner-prompt-gemini.md, partner-prompt.md, prompt-claude-diag.md, prompt-claude-impl.md, prompt-codex.md, prompt-gemini.md, prompt-orchestrator.md. The .md files are session-specific system prompts for the multi-LLM collab feature referenced in the v4 commit subject. The collab.db binary should have been blocked by the .gitignore *.db pattern but was committed while already tracked. Decision needed: (a) remove the entire .collab/ from git history and add .collab/ to .gitignore — these are session runtime artifacts not repo content, OR (b) keep the .md prompts if the collab system is intended to be checked in, but at minimum remove collab.db + gitignore it. CLAUDE.md §hard rules already lists .collab/ as working-tree noise (rule #5). Recommendation: git rm -r .collab/ + add .collab/ to .gitignore. Source: bd site-audit-fix-work-0au forensic.

title: Remove committed .bak files for generate-multipage-report.js (4 locations)
description: Discovered during 0au v4 branch forensic investigation. Four .bak files are tracked in the repo from the v4 commit a139db9 ("feat: v4 — multi-LLM collab audit, retry logic, contentQuality permanent fix", 2026-04-15): template/reports/multipage/generate-multipage-report.js.bak, clients/laura-willis/reports/multipage/generate-multipage-report.js.bak, clients/liane-jamason/reports/multipage/generate-multipage-report.js.bak, clients/matt-wallmow/reports/multipage/generate-multipage-report.js.bak. These are editor/session backup artifacts — the actual .js files were removed by Tier 4 Fix 14 (commit 6bb4dc3) but the .bak copies were left behind. They are currently tracked in site-audit-fixes-tier-4 (inherited from v4). The .gitignore covers clients/*/seo/research/*.json.bak and clients/*/seo/audit-data.json.bak but NOT generate-multipage-report.js.bak pattern — closing this issue should also add a gitignore entry to prevent recurrence. Recommended action: git rm the 4 files + add clients/*/reports/multipage/*.bak and template/reports/multipage/*.bak to .gitignore. Source: bd site-audit-fix-work-0au forensic.

title: Investigate v4 branch artifacts (phantom gitlink discovered during Tier 4)
description: During Tier 4 C2 execution, clients/chris-nevada was found registered as a 160000 gitlink pointing at commit 8832cc2c18149536872e8dbdade48026277b34fc — which does NOT exist in the local git db. No .gitmodules ever existed. Introduced by commit a139db9 ('feat: v4 — multi-LLM collab audit, retry logic, contentQuality permanent fix') on the v4 branch (visible at remotes/origin/v4). Cleaned up via Tier 4 C2-prep commit (34f0801). Action needed: investigate v4 branch for other abandoned submodule-style references or experimental artifacts before any future v4 merge or rebase. Bundle with whoever next touches the v4 branch.
close_reason: v4 forensic complete. Findings: 2 new bd issues filed beyond the known chris-nevada gitlink (already cleaned in tier-4 commit 34f0801). (1) site-audit-fix-work-c6r: 4 committed .bak files for generate-multipage-report.js in template + 3 clients — editor artifacts, .gitignore gap discovered. (2) site-audit-fix-work-8d2: .collab/ directory (10 files, 104KB binary collab.db) committed in v4 — session runtime artifacts not repo content, .gitignore *.db pattern was bypassed because file was already tracked. Both are P3 cleanup items, no code-correctness impact.

title: Reliability sweep: 9 Python connectors bypass _request_sync retry coverage
description: Tier 2 Fix 6 added retry coverage to base._request_sync and routed DataForSEO _post through it. The other 9 sync connectors still call self.sync_client.request()/.post() directly with inline raise_for_status() — no retry coverage for transient failures. Files: connectors/{pagespeed,crux,business_profile,brand_mentions,social_audit,search_console,ga4,google_ads,local_seo}.py. pagespeed.py also has no rate-limit at all. Most natural fit: bundle opportunistically with whatever future fix touches any of these connectors. Source: HANDOFF-POST-TIER-3 Section 5a.

title: Calgary extract-text.js upstream-then-replace
description: Calgary's scripts/extract-text.js is a 275-line fork preserved through Tier 4 sync via sha256-fingerprint guard. Contains Calgary-specific community slugs + richer syllable algorithm + main/article extraction (vs template's body-wide approach). Owner needed: extract universally-useful improvements (syllable algo, main/article extraction) into template; remove Calgary-specific slugs from the fork (or move them to a config-driven mechanism); then sync calgary's extract-text.js. Bundle with whoever next touches extract-text.js or with Tier 5 Fix 16 if it touches the JS gather stack. Source: TIER-4-PLAN Q1.5 + Section 5 NEW item.

value: Spam classifier reframe SIMPLIFIES Fix 16 backlinks decision: with no classifier output needed, choose the path that just gathers and emits the raw list. May tilt other dual-path decisions where classifier complexity was a deciding factor. Per insight 2026-04-29.

Project SOP needed for AI-assisted feature/data additions. Should prevent the dead-code-yet-tested pattern (sentiment analysis ran + tests passed but renderer never displayed it; aj1 made it green for nothing). SOP should require: every new analyzer/feature has a renderer consumer mapping + test that proves the data reaches the report; dead-code purges as part of routine hygiene. Plan toward writing this in Tier 5 or 6, not now. Per user direction 2026-04-29.

Tier 5 pre-commit safety = pre-commit framework (https://pre-commit.com) + .gitignore pattern clients/*/.env. Framework chosen over raw .git/hooks shell script for future-proofing. Per user direction 2026-05-03.

Tier 5+ retired-code archive lives at /root/site-audit-retired/ (separate git repo, sibling to /root/site-audit/ and /root/site-audit-fix-work/). Mirror original paths inside (e.g., site-audit-retired/platform/src/audit_platform/analyzers/backlinks.py). Each retired file should include a header comment with: which tier retired it, what replaced it, why. Keeps main project clean + zero accidental-import risk + preserves optionality. Per user direction 2026-04-29.

Tier 5 spam classifier OMITTED entirely (strengthened from prior reframe). Not a manual-review warning UI either — just OMIT. Renderer's classification fallback heuristics also out. Reasoning: cannot say with absolute certainty that classifications are correct; classifier adds unnecessary complexity layer with false-positive liability. Per user direction 2026-04-29 (supersedes earlier 'reframe as warning' memory).
PPC workflow (Fix 15) is OUT of Tier 5 scope. User building PPC separately to keep organic/PPC segregated and avoid tool wire-crossing. Per user direction 2026-04-29.

Tier 5 JS env-loading = custom lib/load-client-env.js helper (Option B). Reads clients/<slug>/.env via fs.readFileSync, parses KEY=value lines, returns object. Replaces process.env.X with env.X across ~10 gather scripts. Eliminates process.env cross-wire risk at language level. Per user direction 2026-05-03.

Tier 5 OVERRIDING PRINCIPLE: reliability, durability, consistency. Not simplicity. The audit pipeline must work every time. Choose paths with smallest failure surface, fewest false positives, most boring/well-tested patterns. Avoid cleverness. Per user direction 2026-04-29.

Tier 5 Python env-loading = ClientContext class (Option C revised). Wraps pydantic Settings for validation; uses dotenv_values to parse without os.environ pollution. Carries slug + lazy .env load + audit_data_path() helpers. ~40 LOC new code. Per user direction 2026-05-03.

Tier 5 client .env segregation = TOP PRIORITY. Global .env for shared keys ONLY (template for copying, never read by connectors). On new-client creation, copy to clients/<c>/.env. Connectors read CLIENT-LOCAL .env, never global. Goal: zero cross-wire risk between clients (refund risk if Client A pulls Client B's GA4/GSC data). Per user direction 2026-04-29.

Tier 5 dual-path retirement = move to removed/ folder, not delete and not just @deprecated tags. Preserves optionality to learn from the loser or revert if the winner is worse. Per user direction 2026-04-29.
Tier 5 new-client onboarding = build /new-client skill that prompts for client keys and writes clients/<slug>/.env from global .env template. Confirmed scope item. Per user direction 2026-05-03.

Tier 5 spam classifier reframe = drop classify-as-spam-or-not entirely. Surface manual-review WARNING with criteria (legit site, structure, ranking, age). Removes our liability for false-flagging legitimate domains. Same criteria seeds a future v2 classifier. Per user direction 2026-04-29.
